996 GUARDIAN

Automation needs verified outcomes.

A replayable policy workbench derived from real Windows automation failures.

What we built

Independent agents with configurable coordinates and priorities. Each route passes through observe, approach, search, detail confirmation, entry verification and Automatic mode. Missing entrances and unanswered clicks expire within fixed budgets. BOSS timers and token spending run on the same virtual clock.

What runs here

The browser engine controls a deterministic simulator. It sends no game input and has no connection to Windows, a broker or a real account. Imported bundles validate configuration and commands before replay.

Why these policies

Guardian development exposed repeated problems: an entrance was unclear, a click produced no feedback, a stale task held the scheduler, an activity label stayed visible while Automatic was off. The workbench makes those cases reproducible with explicit simulated evidence.

Test plan

Node checks verify policy invariants. TestSprite will exercise the deployed interface: configure agents, start scenarios, advance time, assert failure recovery and verify isolation. A real PR check is required before competition submission. TestSprite setup and submission are still in preparation.

Boundaries

Passing a simulator scenario does not prove that a real game click, OCR read or combat action succeeds. Configurations stay in this browser. The demo is a policy port of GuardianV4.19.12, rather than the original assistant exposed as a web application.
